nonblocking_findings:
(4) Note direction. Checked against the installed reledmac.sty, lines 2984-3051. 
ormalvfootnote is defined [2] and calls 
ormalvfootnote@inserted{#1}{#2} inside \insert\csname #1footins\endcsname{...}. 
ormalvfootnote@inserted [2] runs 
ottoggle{Xgroupbyline@#1}{
oindent} first and ends with \csname #1footfmt\endcsname #2{#1}. 
ormalfootfmt is [4], with #3 as the note text. So \pretocmd puts \OSInspectNoteDirection#2 before the 
oindent. Its #1#2#3 pick up the three brace groups, with #3 brace-stripped. This is correct. All three helpers that take arguments are \long, and an empty #3 or one starting with a brace falls through to \OSSkipNoteDirection safely. The \pardir/	extdir assignment happens inside the \insert group, so it does not leak into the main galley's line boxes. That was the main regression risk, and it does not apply. If the patch fails, the build stops with a PackageError instead of failing silently.

(4) Coverage gaps. These are not regressions. \mpnormalvfootnote@inserted (ledgroup) and the Xgroupbyline path (\add@Xgroupbyline, where \noindent is skipped and notes share one paragraph) are not patched or have no effect. Paragraph-arrangement series (\parafootfmt) also do not get the early \pardir. In all of these, the tag still runs inside the content as an ordinary \pardir/\textdir switch at the note start. For Bendnote the tag is simply set inline. Worth a comment in case those arrangements are ever enabled.

(4) test_reledmac_xslt.py:4550. The weakened assertion \\par(?:\s|[{}]) now misses \par\relax and \par followed directly by another control sequence. Use \\par(?![A-Za-z@]) so \pardir is excluded and every real \par token is still caught.

(3) Conditional bracket space. The logic is right for the source and prefix cases, and the rendered test confirms both '[inside] after.' and '[pre]fix.'. Edge cases where the space is still lost: (a) the following sibling is an element whose string value is empty or starts later, e.g. an adjacent <j:conditional/> start, a milestone, or an anchor, as in 'x <end/><cond/>y'; (b) the following text starts with an initial quote (\p{Pi}, e.g. “), a geresh/gershayim, or other punctuation not in \p{Ps}. Consider using following::text()[normalize-space()][1] or a following-sibling that skips empty milestones, and adding \p{Pi}. Also, a whitespace-only preceding sibling (pretty-printed XML) counts as a source space. That is semantically defensible, but note that it changes output.

(2) Spanning headings. \OSApplyKeep → \vspace is a valid keep: glue after a penalty is not a legal break. But the \begin{hebrew} write whatsit comes before the glue, so the half-baseline space is not discarded when the heading starts a page. Expect an extra ~0.5\baselineskip at the page top in that case. Also, with \par, whatsit, \nobreak and \vspace in sequence, the only legal break before the heading has to come from glue or a penalty at the end of the preceding columns material. That was already true before this change, but a geometry assertion for 'heading at page top' / 'previous last line not dragged' would guard it.

(5) Interlinear mark. \ht\strutbox follows \baselineskip (0.7·bs), not the actual glyph height. It clears Hebrew enlarged with \fontsize, but not Hebrew scaled through a fontspec Scale= or similar without a baselineskip change. The \raisebox height also adds to the line's height: raise plus mark height is now about 0.2em more than before. Unless the interlinear band reserves that much, lines carrying a mark may get \lineskip and parallel rows may drift. Check that baselines are evenly spaced on a mark-bearing line, or \smash the raised box if the band is already reserved.

(1) Deferred f:block-break \pstart. This is correct, and the structural test confirms 105 \pstart and 35 chapter marks. A trailing break with no following content no longer risks an empty \pstart. The test does not cover the role label being nearer its own row than the previous one, as the earlier reviewer noted.
Minor: test_reledmac_xslt.py:2999 raises a SyntaxWarning for '\p' in a non-raw docstring. Make it a raw string.
limitations: This was a static review. I did not run lualatex, pytest or the proof myself. I relied on the logs provided: 507 passed and 218 subtests in the regression log, and 2 passed in the geometry log.

I verified the reledmac argument shape against the installed /usr/share/texlive/.../reledmac.sty. I did not check reledpar's column/pages paths, or whether print@Xcomponents or footnotelang@lua reset \pardir when enabled.

I did not see the XSLT around the spanning-heading, block-break and conditional hunks, beyond the diff context. In particular, I did not check whether $single-pstart is named consistently with the 'paired eager / full-width deferred' description, or what \OSApplyKeep and \OSCondEndInline expand to.
The keep-together suite rerun and the full-volume final export are still pending, and this approval does not cover them.
